text:
sasha: FYI — I'm wiring a 'per-model cost lens' for the console. Need input on how routing weight + cache credits should be surfaced. Should we show: (A) effective token unit cost after routing and cache, or (B) raw per-model token cost + separate overlay for routing multiplier and cache savings? cc @morgan @raj

morgan: my vote B. separate layers are easier to reason about in rollouts. show per-canary vs prod routing weights too. :+1:

raj: agree with morgan. also we need sampling controls — computing exact attribution for every single invocation is prohibitively expensive. propose sample 1% and extrapolate, show CI bands so folks know uncertainty. :thinking_face:

emily: UX question — where do quotas live in this model? per-model or per-route? if quotas are per-route the dashboard needs to surface "sticky routing" cost impact and quota burn projections.

keegan: quick sketch of the attribution query we used for prefetch/cache credits: 
```sql
SELECT model,
       SUM(tokens * unit_cost) AS raw_cost,
       SUM(cache_saved_tokens * unit_cost) AS cache_savings
FROM invocations
WHERE ts > now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY model;
```
We then apply routing_weight multipliers per route to report an "effective_cost" for each route+model combination. Keep the raw numbers available for audits.

sasha: neat. UX: how do we preview canary effects? inline toggle that simulates routing weights with a slider and shows delta to bill and micros/token. maybe also a "what-if" overlay that runs the sampled projection.

morgan: yes — a "what-if slider" is gold. show sample rate and CI, and expose the sample provenance (which sampler id / materialized-view generation). backend should emit provenance tags so console can link back to the MV or sample job.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started: routing-change/2026-03-21 — 10% -> 20% to model-x

raj: small nit: when showing cache savings prefer absolute $ saved + percentage and also normalize per-token (micros/token) so product folks can compare across model families.

emily: accessibility note — choose a colorblind-friendly palette for delta heatmap and don't rely on color alone for sign (+/-).

keegan: implementation note: keep heavy joins in an offline materialized view refreshed every 5-15m. live path should read MV + a small tail sampler for the most recent minutes to avoid blocking queries.

sasha: OK I'll prototype a Figma mock and post to #eng-platform-design for review. plan to include a "show raw vs effective" toggle and the what-if slider.

morgan: +1. If anyone wants to pair on the SQL/materialization or sampler, ping me.

raj: thanks — tagging product analytics for visibility on aggregated billing exports: @product-analytics
